paragraphs: GIFT Nifty is at 22998.5, down 60.5 points or 0.26 percent, implying a muted start for the domestic session compared to Nifty's last close of 22936.75. Bank Nifty closed at 54909.65 and India VIX finished the previous session at 15.12.

Overnight, Wall Street closed in the red with the S&P 500 down 0.30 percent at 7720.39, the Nasdaq down 1.38 percent at 26184.725, and the Dow Jones lower by 0.25 percent at 52342.56. US futures currently point lower, led by Nasdaq futures dropping 2.06 percent to 28953.75 and S&P 500 futures losing 0.94 percent to 7681.0. Across Asia, markets are facing sharp losses with Kospi plunging 5.48 percent to 5612.09, Taiwan down 4.47 percent to 44934.63, Nikkei 225 down 2.54 percent to 63019.78, and Shanghai dropping 1.50 percent to 3626.199, while Hang Seng bucked the trend to rise 0.93 percent to 23310.4. In Europe, the DAX closed up 1.31 percent at 26039.68 and the FTSE 100 gained 0.26 percent to 10722.07.

In commodities, Brent crude jumped to 112.15 with a 1.22 percent gain, while WTI crude advanced 1.27 percent to 103.3. Gold is trading at 4010.6, down 0.52 percent, and Silver fell 1.52 percent to 51.585. Copper eased 0.55 percent to 6.5665 and Natural gas declined 1.76 percent to 2.9. Currency and rates show USD/INR at 95.2, down 0.01 percent, the Dollar index lower by 0.28 percent at 101.748, and the US 10Y yield at 4.989.

In the cash market, FIIs sold Rs 943.6 crore while DIIs bought Rs 1924.41 crore on 2026-10-29. Over the last five sessions, FIIs total a positive flow of Rs 3593.78 crore and DIIs total Rs 7162.66 crore. Call walls stand heavy at the 23500.0 strike with 11855935.0 open interest, while put walls show strong concentration at 22000.0 with 9816625.0 open interest. ATM IV is recorded at 12.99. KAYNES and SAIL are currently under the F&O ban list.

Today's heavy corporate calendar features Q2 results from Reliance, Jio Platforms, Sun Pharma, Dixon, BEL, IOC, BoB, GAIL, GE Vernova, Lodha, Max Health, Delhivery, Aether, and NTPC Green, amongst a massive queue of earnings. Key macroeconomic events include the Bank of Japan Policy Rate, Monetary Policy Statement, BOJ Outlook Report, and BOJ Press Conference at 08:00–11:00 IST, alongside the US Employment Cost Index q/q later in the day.

Top news items focus on a massive lineup of Q2 results driving stock-specific volatility across Energy, Pharma, Banking, and Infrastructure. Crude oil spiked to $118 amid geopolitical tensions, posing inflation risks for Oil & Gas and the broad market. Additionally, the Supreme Court cracked down on banks by seeking mandatory payouts to cyber fraud victims, impacting Banking, while the RBI raised the Floating Rate Bond 2034 interest rate by 81 basis points. Credit card spending fell nearly 6 percent in September, marking the first decline since February 2021 and hitting Financials.
